title: Telemetry contract marshal for console usage pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The console usage ingestion pipeline currently experiences intermittent event rejections and silent drops when SDKs emit variants of the usage event contract. Root causes include brittle schema checks in the ingestion lambda, lack of formal schema evolution rules, and inconsistent normalization across sources (hosted API, Dedicated, Private connectors). This leads to skewed billing/usage dashboards and increased operational toil from ad-hoc fixes.

Goal: Build a lightweight, centrally managed "Telemetry Contract Marshal" service that performs: (1) contract validation for incoming usage events, (2) progressive normalization (mapping legacy/variant fields to canonical contract), (3) compatibility checking against a schema registry, and (4) safe failure modes with DLQ + sampled replay. The marshal should be small-latency for critical fields and offload heavy validation/enrichment to async pipeline stages.

Non-goals: This ticket does not cover end-to-end UI dashboard changes or billing reconciliation logic; those follow-ups live in the Console Observability epic.

Design summary:
- Front-door: lightweight HTTP/gRPC marshal deployed as a console-backend service behind API Gateway for internal sources and as a dedicated ingest endpoint for internal connectors.
- Validation: use a type-driven schema registry (json-schema + typed validators) with explicit backward/forward compatibility rules. Each schema version includes metadata: allowed aliases, normalization rules, and deprecation windows.
- Runtime modes: "strict" for internal QA clusters, "recommended" (default) which soft-fails non-critical fields and attaches warnings, and "permissive" for legacy customer streams.
- Performance: synchronous checks limited to presence/format of critical keys (customer_id, timestamp, route, token_type). Heavy checks (semantic validations, large arrays) run asynchronously in the pipeline worker with structured error tagging. Target p50 validation latency < 15ms for synchronous path.
- Failure handling: Rejected events go to a DLQ bucket with automatic sampling to a debug index. For soft-fail cases, events pass through with an attached _schema_warnings array. Operators get counters and example payloads in the console.
- Observability: histograms for validation latency, counters for validation outcomes by rule, sampled payloads, and alerting for rising rejection-rate > 0.5% over baseline.

Why this approach: Balances developer velocity (quick schema changes via registry), operational safety (soft-fail + DLQ), and cost (avoid heavyweight per-event work). Trade-offs: adds a hop and CPU cost; mitigated by small binary and pooling, and heavy validations moved to async workers.

Deliverables: design doc + confluence page, schema registry prototype, marshal service (Go), lambda ingest adapter for legacy connectors, dashboards and alerts, migration runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Marshal endpoint validates and normalizes incoming usage events for 3 canonical schema versions
Critical-field synchronous validation p50 < 15ms and p95 < 60ms in staging under 200rps
Events failing strict validation are written to DLQ with sample debug payloads
Soft-failging behavior attaches _schema_warnings and increments metrics instead of dropping events
Automated compatibility checks in schema registry with a one-click promote workflow
Runbook for migrating legacy connectors and a scheduled rollout plan validated in staging
steps: Draft design doc and run trade-off analysis (proto: Confluence link)
Prototype schema registry and compatibility rules (json-schema + codegen)
Implement marshal service and unit/property tests (Go)
Add lambda adapter for Private/Dedicated connectors + integration tests
Add dashboards, example payload sampler, and alert rules in Grafana/Alertmanager
Canary rollout to internal QA cluster, then staged rollout to production connectors
Post-mortem and measurement of rejection rates vs baseline
comments: 2025-11-04 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes: decide on json-schema + lightweight codegen for validators. Mateo to prototype a validator microservice and measure latency.

2025-11-06 - Mateo Rivera: Prototype validator implemented; initial sync-only validation of 4 critical fields has median 8ms in local load harness. Observed p95 spike when validating large metadata arrays—plan to move arrays to async path.
2025-11-08 - Priya Menon (PM): Reviewed; requested explicit compatibility policy doc and a default 'recommended' mode for hosted customers to avoid accidental drops.

2025-11-11 - Design review (internal): Agreed to include field aliases table to handle legacy SDK payloads. Design note: don't attempt to canonicalize deeply nested customer metadata at intake—do in enrichment stage.

2025-11-14 - Security review (triage): Telemetry payloads may contain PII in free-form metadata. Decision: marshal must include PII redaction hooks and redact-sampling for debug payloads. Security follow-up: add data classification tooling to registry. (security_review_required=false for this ticket; separate security follow-up created)

2025-11-17 - Mateo Rivera: Integration test with Dedicated connector passes; DLQ entries written and sample replay tool can rehydrate events into staging pipeline. Preparing canary rollout plan for 2025-11-20.
2025-11-19 - Aisha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to include SLA and migration runbook tasks. Assigned follow-ups for billing reconciliation team to validate counters.
notes: Keep schema registry formats stable and human-readable; include changelog and promotion timestamps.
We will rely on existing event-canonicalizer work (ENG-10821) for enrichment stage mappings.
DLQ storage should be versioned and retention-configurable; default 30d for debug artifacts.
